notes: Low-fidelity programmes (JiSEF mean 80.1, SD 6.5; 7 programmes). Construct is paid_competitive, not paid_any: only competitive employment evidenced by an employment contract was counted, so any sheltered or welfare-office work is excluded and paid_any is not identified. The 93 is NEITHER a reporting base NOR an observed denominator, and the triage note's framing of it as a denominator question needs that correction: 'During the recruitment period, 93 clients met the inclusion criteria, and 51 were included in the analyses' (Results, p. 477). 93 is a count of clients meeting the eligibility criteria; no percentage in the paper divides by it, so it is not a reporting base, and no outcome was observed for all 93, so it is not an observed denominator. The reporting base and the observed denominator are both 29 and 22, on which every printed percentage reproduces exactly (11/29 = 37.9, 15/22 = 68.2, 6/29 = 20.7, 13/22 = 59.1, 12/22 = 54.5). n_entered is left BLANK because the report does not say how many of the 93 consented and entered, and the flow diagram that would say is in an online supplement not held. The 42 unaccounted-for clients are why analysis_selection_status = unclear rather than none: whether they were non-consenters, dropouts or excluded for some employment-related reason cannot be established. Ascertainment is cumulative, not point prevalence: the Table 2 row is 'N of people who worked / During the past 12 months', which counts anyone meeting the definition at any point in the follow-up. Job tenure and retention are registered outcomes designated narrative-only (SAP section 2.3) and are recorded here rather than as separate result rows, because the schema has no job-tenure construct: maintained the initial job throughout the study period, 1 year after starting work, 6 of 29 (20.7 per cent) low-fidelity and 13 of 22 (59.1 per cent) high-fidelity; maintained the last job throughout the study period, 6 of 29 (20.7 per cent) and 12 of 22 (54.5 per cent); mean work tenure 56.4 (SD 101.0) and 166.2 (SD 135.0) days; mean days to the first job 298.2 (SD 107.1) and 190.5 (SD 140.1). The retention counts are anchored to each individual's job start date and extend beyond the 12-month follow-up ('we collected information about whether the participants maintained their employment for 1 year after starting their job, which was beyond the 12-month follow-up period. Data collection was completed in December 2017'). perc_employed_baseline is deliberately BLANK. Table 1 prints 'Job experience in past 6 months' (3 of 29 and 2 of 22), which is prior work experience, not employment at baseline, and typing it into a baseline-employment moderator would misstate the moderator. n_post_secondary is also blank: the education categories are Secondary / High school / Vocational school / Junior college / University, and whether Japanese vocational school counts as post-secondary is a classification judgement the source does not make. Low-fidelity: 3 / 16 / 4 / 1 / 5 of 29; high-fidelity: 3 / 8 / 2 / 2 / 7 of 22. n_female is the exact complement of the printed male counts (Table 1 lists only Male, 23 of 29 and 13 of 22, against the stated group totals), not a back-calculation from a percentage.

outcome_verbatim: 'At 15-mo follow-up, 34 (63.0%) of ISE participants had obtained competitive employment, compared with 27 (50.0%) of IPS and 18 (33.3%) of TVR participants.' 'Competitive employment referred to work at a full-time or part-time job in the free job market to which anyone could apply, and the salary was based on the market value and paid directly by the employers (Mak et al., 2006). Those who had continuously held competitive employment at least 20 hr/wk for 2 mo or longer were considered employed. The cumulative employment rate at different follow-up periods was also reported.'
source_locator: Results, Employment Rates, p. 7106165020p5; outcome definition in Method, Data Collection and Analysis, p. 7106165020p4; corroborated in the Abstract, p. 7106165020p1 (63.0%, 50.0%, 33.3%)
notes: Integrated supported employment arm (IPS plus work-related social skills training). Construct is paid_intensity_threshold, NOT paid_competitive and certainly not paid_any: a participant counts as employed only if they held competitive work continuously for at least 20 hours a week for two months or longer, so everyone working fewer hours or for a shorter spell is counted as not employed. The labour-market setting is competitive and is preserved in the verbatim, but the threshold changes the numerator while keeping a paid-employment label, which is what D12.3a exists to stop; the number in any competitive employment is not identified and is bounded 34 <= x <= 54 in the ISE arm, 27 <= x <= 54 in IPS and 18 <= x <= 54 in TVR. Ascertainment is any_time_during_followup, confirming the triage note: the figure is the cumulative employment rate over follow-up, not point prevalence at 15 months. No point-prevalence count is printed at any timepoint. DENOMINATOR: n_outcome_observed is BLANK and 54 is recorded as n_entered and as reported_percentage_base. The authors state 'The participants (n = 162) were subject to intent-to-treat analyses on employment rate ... The drop-out cases were also included', which establishes that dropouts occurred and were counted in the denominator, but the report gives NO attrition figure anywhere, no flow diagram, and no statement of how employment status was obtained for those who dropped out. Printed percentages establish what the authors divided by, not that the outcome was observed for that many people (prompt rule 7), so 54 goes to reported_percentage_base and denominator_basis = entered. Without n_outcome_observed the row cannot enter the count model of SAP section 10.2; this is the batch's most consequential author query (unresolved_queries.md Q10). No whole-cohort (arm_type = cohort) row is created for this trial. Merging the three arms would fail the SAP section 2.1 safeguard employment_targeted_intervention, since every arm received a vocational intervention intended to change employment, and the cohort is employment-selected in any case. TIMEPOINT: followup_months = 15 measured from admission, which the assessment schedule establishes ('assessments at admission (baseline); at completion of the 3-mo program; and at 7-, 11-, and 15-mo follow-up'). One ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved: 'assessments at the 7th month after joining the program were operationally adopted as the baseline for the vocational outcomes including employment rate', so the window over which cumulative employment was accumulated may be months 7 to 15 rather than 0 to 15. That does not change the timepoint but leaves the length of the accumulation window unknown. 15 months falls in the 9-to-18-month band and would be assigned to the 12-month horizon under D11.1; the cumulative ascertainment and the allocated arm type keep it out of the primary pool regardless. Moderators: mean_age and n_female are per arm from Table 1. Education is printed as Junior secondary / Senior secondary / Tertiary, so post-secondary is identified exactly as the Tertiary count. Baseline employment is not a moderator here: all participants were unemployed at entry by eligibility criterion (3), so perc_employed_baseline is 0 by construction and is recorded as a count with its denominator; Table 1's 'Work experience' row (29, 30 and 33 of 54) is PRIOR work experience, not baseline employment, and is not used for that field.
